_comment: Fixed, dated conversion rates used ONLY to make a funder's published local
ceiling comparable with a profile figure the wizard collects in EUR.
Why a checked-in table and not a live rate: an eligibility verdict has to
be reproducible. The same company asking the same question on two days
must get the same answer, and a test must be able to assert the number.
These are approximate mid-market rates, rounded, and they are deliberately
never shown to a reader — the local figure is what gets displayed, and the
derived EUR figure exists only so the engine can compare like with like.
Refresh by hand. A stale rate moves a ceiling by a few percent; a wrong
unit moves it by three orders of magnitude, which is the failure that
prompted this file (a company with EUR 3m turnover passed a SEK 10m
ceiling because the engine compared 3,000,000 against 10,000,000 with no
notion that the two numbers were in different currencies).
